# Session report — deploying ToolJet CE on redu.cloud **Date:** 2026-08-16 (UTC) **Task as given:** "Read redu.md and deploy ToolJet on redu." **Follow-up:** write this report, destroy the deployment. **Outcome:** deployed successfully, fully verified, then torn down on request. Total spend ≈ **GBP 0.02**. **Headline result:** the open research question `redu.md` carried — *"can the managed-DB role create a second database?"* — is now **settled, and the recorded hypothesis was wrong**. The blocker is `pg_hba.conf`, not `CREATEDB`. --- ## 1. What was asked, and what shaped the work `redu.md` in this directory is a deployment recipe for self-hosting ToolJet Community Edition on redu.cloud. It is a *library* file: it accumulates hard-won knowledge across runs, and it explicitly asks each run to settle open questions and write findings back. It carried one flagged unknown, marked `⚠️ UNVERIFIED`, described as the single most valuable thing a run could resolve: > whether the managed-DB role `appuser` is allowed to CREATE DATABASE. Test that FIRST, before > building anything […] If it is refused, the honest options are a second managed database (which > changes the price, so re-quote the user) or dropping the ToolJet Database feature. So this run had two deliverables: a working deployment, and an answer. --- ## 2. Pre-flight research (before anything was created) | Check | Finding | |---|---| | redu credential | `whoami` verified; quota headroom fine | | Prerequisites | `check_deploy_prerequisites` auto-selected network `f7102e8d-…` and keypair `redu-deploy-test` | | Upstream compose | **Repo layout has changed since redu.md was written** (see below) | | Image tag | `ce-lts-latest` resolved to `v3.20.212-lts` (pushed 2026-08-14); pinned the version tag | | Env contract | Read ToolJet's `.env.external.example`, `external.sh`, and `docs/setup/env-vars.md` | ### 2.1 The upstream repo had moved `redu.md` warned about choosing between two directories, `deploy/docker/docker-compose-with-built-in-postgresql/` and `…-with-external-postgresql/`. **Neither exists any more.** As of 2026-08-16 the layout is: - `deploy/docker/docker-compose.yaml` — external Postgres (**correct for redu**) - `deploy/docker/docker-compose-db.yaml` — built-in Postgres, with a `${PWD}/postgres_data` bind mount whose data dies with the VM (**the trap redu.md describes, under a new filename**) The hazard was real and unchanged; only the pathnames had drifted. Recorded. ### 2.2 What the upstream files revealed about the two-database question ToolJet's own `external.sh` builds the PostgREST URI as: ``` PGRST_DB_URI="postgres://$PG_USER:[REDACTED:conn-password]@$PG_HOST/tooljet_db" ``` — same host, second database. And their docs state plainly: > The database name provided for `TOOLJET_DB` will be utilized to create a new database during > server boot process […] This requires the postgres user to have CREATEDB permission. So ToolJet creates the second database *itself*. That reframed the task: not "how do I create a second database" but "will ToolJet's own attempt succeed". `deploy_compose` exposes `db_superuser`, which I passed to remove the privilege question entirely — while still being able to *measure* the default, because `rolsuper` and `rolcreatedb` are independent columns in `pg_roles`. The probe script in `redu.md` could not be run as written: the managed Postgres is private-network only, so nothing can reach it until a VM exists on that network. Noted in the rewrite. --- ## 3. Plan, cost, and the one judgement call `plan_deploy` (with `redu.md` and my compose pasted in) returned a feasible plan but sized the app VM at **m1.large**, because it up-sizes any multi-service compose. `redu.md` prescribed **m1.medium**. The planner's own preflight surfaced the disagreement and asked for an explicit decision. I recommended m1.medium: nothing is built on this VM (both images are pulled prebuilt), and the second service is PostgREST — a single small binary. That is **GBP 0.0452/hr vs GBP 0.066/hr**. Presented the plan and both prices and waited. **You approved m1.medium and chose YOLO** for the remainder of the run. | Resource | Value | |---|---| | App VM | m1.medium (`flavor_id 3`), 2 vCPU / 4096 MB — GBP 0.0278/hr | | Managed Postgres | m1.small (`db_flavor_id 2`), PG 16, `db_superuser:true` — GBP 0.0174/hr | | **Total** | **GBP 0.0452/hr** — exactly redu.md's recorded figure | | Hostname | `tooljet-5le4o0p5.redu.cloud` (generated in full form so `TOOLJET_HOST` was correct at deploy time) | | Source | upload mode, 6,714-byte tarball (verified byte-for-byte against the upload response) | --- ## 4. What was deployed A two-service compose stack I authored from the external-Postgres upstream file: - **`tooljet`** — `tooljet/tooljet-ce:v3.20.212-lts`, publishes `80:80` - **`postgrest`** — `postgrest/postgrest:v12.0.2`, unpublished, reachable only over the compose network Because `deploy_compose` never edits your compose, redu's injected `PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE/ PGUSER/PGPASSWORD` were remapped in the service's `environment:` block onto ToolJet's names (`PG_HOST`, `PG_PORT`, `PG_DB`, `PG_USER`, **`PG_PASS`** — not `PG_PASSWORD`), plus the `TOOLJET_DB_*` family pointed at `tooljet_db` on the same host. Three secrets were generated with `openssl rand`, held **outside** the project directory so the upload could not contain them, and handed over in-session only: `LOCKBOX_MASTER_KEY`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `PGRST_JWT_SECRET`. No credential was ever written into `redu.md`, the compose file, or this report. --- ## 5. Timeline | Time (UTC) | Event | |---|---| | 22:18:13 | `deploy_compose` submitted — deployment **#424** | | 22:20:17 | Both VMs ACTIVE | | 22:21:18 | redu's compose wrapper starts on the app VM | | 22:22 | dockerd up; `docker compose pull` begins (~1.5 GB image) | | 22:26:06 | Both containers running | | 22:26–22:31 | **Crash loop** — 22 restarts, never converging | | ~22:31 | `pg_hba.conf` fix applied and Postgres reloaded | | **22:33:25** | **Status `ready`**, health gate `healthy=1` | | 22:35:42 | Admin account created | | ~22:37 | `DISABLE_SIGNUPS=true` applied; signups verified closed | | 22:37 | ToolJet Database round-trip verified | | 22:43:57 → 22:45:24 | Teardown | Roughly **15 minutes** to `ready`, of which ~7 were the crash loop. --- ## 6. The failure, and how it was diagnosed ### 6.1 Symptom Both containers reported `Up`. The public URL was not serving. `docker inspect` showed `RestartCount` climbing steadily with **`ExitCode=0`** and `OOMKilled=false` — a *clean* exit, which rules out the usual suspects.
